title: Gartner Identifies the Top Trends for Data and Analytics
summary: Six D&A trends for 2026: sovereign AI, decision governance for agents, AI governance platforms, agentic data streaming (forecast to exceed 60% adoption by 2028 from under 15% in 2025), agentic data management and GraphRAG (40% of enterprises by 2029). Agents, semantics and converged platforms named as the driving forces.

title: Gartner Announces Top Predictions for Data and Analytics in 2026
summary: Predicts universal semantic layers become critical infrastructure by 2030; half of organisations using agents to turn governance policy into data contracts by 2030; half of agent failures due to weak runtime governance by 2030; 75% of hiring to test AI proficiency by 2027; physical-world agents generating 10x more data than digital AI by 2029.

title: Open Semantic Interchange (OSI) Updates: Specification Now Live
summary: First OSI specification released under Apache 2 licence; working group expanded to include Databricks, Qlik, AtScale and others alongside Salesforce, dbt Labs, BlackRock and Instacart. Plan to move to foundation governance.
notes: Vendor blog, but reports a multi-vendor standards milestone.

title: Apache Ossie and Apache Polaris: Putting Semantic Models in the Open Catalog
summary: OSI accepted into the Apache Incubator on 10 July 2026 and renamed Apache Ossie, with more than 50 organisations behind it; describes early work to store semantic models in the Polaris catalogue.
notes: Practitioner write-up; incubation date should be confirmed on apache.org.

title: The Apache Iceberg Market in the Middle of 2026
summary: Iceberg Summit 2026 had no sessions arguing for adoption; competition has moved to catalogues, table maintenance and governing access by agents.
notes: Practitioner view; publication date approximate.

title: Data lake architecture design patterns
summary: Cites a 2026 State of Data Engineering survey of 1,101 practitioners: 44% primarily on cloud data warehouses, 27% on lakehouse architectures. Suggests convergence is gradual.
notes: Moderating evidence; primary survey not located.

title: Stanford AI Index 2026 report: 5 key insights
summary: Coverage of the AI Index: OSWorld agent task success up from about 12% to about 66%; US lead over best Chinese model 2.7 points; generative AI at 53% population adoption; 14-26% productivity gains in support and software; entry-level developer jobs (22-25) down 20%.
notes: Verify figures against the primary PDF at hai.stanford.edu.

title: Stanford AI Index 2026 coverage
summary: Reports the AI Index finding that models meet or exceed human baselines on PhD-level science, competition maths and multimodal reasoning.
notes: Verify against primary report.

title: Stanford AI Index 2026 key takeaways
summary: Reports the Foundation Model Transparency Index average falling from 58 to 40 out of 100.
notes: Low-tier secondary source; replace with primary citation on next run.

title: LLM inference prices have fallen rapidly but unequally across tasks
summary: Price of reaching a fixed capability level has fallen between 9x and 900x per year depending on task; GPT-4-level performance on PhD science questions fell about 40x per year.

title: The Price of Progress: Algorithmic Efficiency and the Falling Cost of AI Inference
summary: Frontier inference cost at fixed benchmark performance falls 5-10x per year, yet the cost of running frontier-level models has risen roughly exponentially.

title: The state of AI in 2026: On the road to ROI
summary: Survey of 1,719 respondents: 80% report personal productivity gains but only 37% report any EBIT impact, flat year on year; high performers steady at about 6%; 40% of large firms scaling agents, up from 27%; about 20% constrained by AI operating costs; coding agents driving build over buy.

title: Gartner Predicts Over 40% of Agentic AI Projects Will Be Canceled by End of 2027
summary: Over 40% of agentic projects expected to be cancelled by end-2027 on cost, value and risk; widespread agent washing with only about 130 genuine vendors; still forecasts 15% of daily decisions autonomous and 33% of enterprise apps with agentic AI by 2028.

title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Tasks
summary: Length of tasks frontier agents complete autonomously at 50% reliability has doubled roughly every 7 months for six years.

title: METR Time Horizons: Now 10x/Year
summary: Summarises METR's Time Horizon 1.1 update: for 2024-25 models the doubling time is about 3.5-4 months.
notes: Confirm against METR's own publication.

title: Linux Foundation launches Agentic AI open standards hub
summary: Linux Foundation created the Agentic AI Foundation as neutral home for Model Context Protocol, goose and AGENTS.md.

title: A2A joins AAIF's open agentic stack
summary: Agent2Agent protocol becomes a hosted AAIF project; more than 150 partner organisations including competitors; Google Cloud and PayPal extending it to agent payments via AP2.

title: Google-backed agentic A2A protocol gets a new home
summary: Reports A2A moving to the AAIF; foundation membership reported to have grown from under 40 to over 250 in eight months.
notes: Membership figure via secondary summary of Axios report.

title: IATA Highlights Priorities to Create Value from Digitalization
summary: AI assistants and agents changing how travellers discover and compare travel; airlines urged to keep control of data and customer relationships; seven airlines live or implementing Orders, more than 20 from 2027; IT providers committed over US$1.7bn to Offers and Orders.

title: IATA: Nearly half of air passengers use AI for travel planning
summary: 49% of passengers have used AI for travel planning; Europe lowest region at 35%, Middle East highest at 72%; IATA urges airlines to ensure offers appear in AI tools and convert AI conversations to bookings.
notes: Replace with IATA primary release when located.

title: Fact Sheet - Fulfilling with Orders: ONE Order
summary: Early ONE Order implementers expect better offer optimisation, lower commercial system costs and a foundation ready for agentic AI distribution.

title: The EU's Digital Omnibus on AI: What the Provisional Agreement Really Changes
summary: Provisional agreement of 7 May 2026 delays standalone high-risk AI Act obligations to 2 December 2027 and product-embedded obligations to 2 August 2028.
notes: Prohibited practices and GPAI rules unaffected per other law-firm briefings.

title: Lufthansa Group Capital Markets Day 2025
summary: Airline group plans to remove around 4,000 administrative roles by 2030 through digitalisation, automation and process consolidation, focused on administrative rather than operational roles.
notes: Public airline disclosure used as industry evidence.

title: Gartner's top tech trends for 2027
summary: Gartner's ten 2027 strategic trends include AI context platforms (semantics in AI-ready data to lift agent accuracy by up to 80% and cut costs up to 60% by 2027), AI agent identity (25% of breaches traced to agent abuse by 2028), sovereign tech (over 75% of non-US firms with sovereignty strategies by 2030), world models and an AI coding agent harness.
notes: Gartner primary page returned 403; figures confirmed by narrow fetch of this coverage and cross-checked against a CXOToday reprint of the release.

title: What's new across Google's Agentic Data Cloud
summary: Google positions its Knowledge Catalog as the semantic and business-context layer for agents, grounding them in semantic models from several BI and platform vendors, and adds Iceberg catalogue federation across rival catalogues with cross-cloud access.
notes: Vendor announcement of own products; accuracy and token claims are vendor benchmarks.

title: Oracle adds a semantic layer to ground AI agents in the business context
summary: Oracle announces a business semantic layer for its AI lakehouse to ground agents in governed metrics, plus write access to Iceberg tables via external catalogues.  Analysts quoted warn of maintenance burden and lock-in from proprietary semantic layers.

title: Apache Ossie project site
summary: Project site confirms Ossie entered the Apache Incubator under that name on 10 July 2026; latest dated news is a new participant in August 2026.  The sample specification is still versioned 0.x, so the standard remains pre-1.0.
notes: Published date is the latest dated entry on the site; no news in the lookback window.

title: Confluent Intelligence Q3 2026 update
summary: Confluent reports general availability of a real-time context engine that serves streaming data to agents over MCP, with event-triggered agents and time-series models in Flink in early access.
notes: Vendor announcement of own products; streaming-for-agents evidence remains vendor-heavy.

title: Digital rulebook: simplification of EU data protection and cyber rules
summary: Law-firm briefing: the Council agreed its Digital Omnibus position on 21 October 2026, keeping the GDPR definition of personal data, adding a test for when pseudonymised data is personal, consolidating data-sharing rules and clarifying AI-training legal bases.  Trilogues await Parliament.

title: EU member states finalize Digital Omnibus negotiating stance
summary: The Council position rejects the Commission's proposed redefinition of personal data, narrows cookie-consent changes and prefers national incident-reporting entry points; Parliament has not yet adopted its position.

title: Gartner: ignore data culture and 60% of AI governance efforts will fail by 2027
summary: Gartner predicts that by 2027, 60% of organisations neglecting cultural challenges in data and analytics governance will fail to govern AI; its survey of data and analytics leaders ranks cultural resistance above funding as a barrier.
notes: Underlying Gartner release dated 2026-09-21; figures confirmed by narrow fetch of this coverage.  Bears on the AI-ready data gap noted for human review in proposals/pending.md.

title: AI-ready data research
summary: Survey of 2,000 firms in 15 countries: only 7% have the data readiness needed to scale advanced or agentic AI, and most at least occasionally delay or limit AI because of data risks.
notes: Consultancy survey not on the tier 1 list; treated as tier 4.

title: Comparison of GraphRAG and agentic dense retrieval
summary: Finds that agentic multi-round search largely closes the gap between dense retrieval and GraphRAG; graph-based retrieval keeps an edge mainly on complex multi-hop questions and only where construction cost is amortised.
notes: Contradicts only the GraphRAG strand of DM-01, not the case for semantic layers.

title: Assessment of AI R&D acceleration at Anthropic
summary: High-access assessment estimates frontier progress on well-specified tasks at roughly 1.9x the 2024-25 trend (95% CI 1.5-2.8x), mostly attributed to AI used in AI research.  The estimate drops to about 1.4x on non-Anthropic data and much underlying evidence was redacted.
notes: Figures confirmed by narrow fetch; post corrected on 2026-11-06.

title: Time horizons tracker
summary: METR says its time-horizon page is no longer actively updated and that readings above about 16 hours are unreliable with the current task suite, so frontier agents have outrun the benchmark.
notes: Supports the direction of AG-01 but signals that the main measurement has saturated.

title: Frontier model releases and price cuts, September 2026
summary: New frontier models from two labs shipped weeks apart with list-price cuts of 20% and 50% on predecessors, while third-party per-task costs for top reasoning settings remain around a dollar per task.
notes: Prices are vendor list prices reported by the press.

title: Big 5 AI vendor roundup, week of 2 November 2026
summary: Digest reports OpenAI releasing a cyber-specialised model only to selected defenders, rated at its critical cyber threshold, and an amended IPO filing from Anthropic disclosing very large multi-year compute commitments.
notes: News digest of vendor announcements and filings; verify figures against primary filings.

title: Companies' financial value from AI holds firm in 2026
summary: Coverage of McKinsey State of AI 2026: large firms scaling agents in at least one function rose from 27% to 40%, while the share reporting any EBIT impact (37%) and the high-performer share (about 6%) were flat.
notes: Secondary coverage of the study already in EV-0012; not independent of it.  Confirms its figures by narrow fetch because mckinsey.com returned 503.

title: AI is starting to pay off
summary: Survey of 1,330 executives: about half of companies now report meaningful AI value (7.5% future-built plus 41% scaling), AI spend roughly doubled to about 3.3% of revenue, and agentic AI is forecast to deliver about 40% of AI value by 2030.
notes: Partly contradicts AI-03, but BCG changed its definition of value since 2025, so the year-on-year rise is not like-for-like.

title: Digital AI Omnibus delays key deadlines, introduces new rules
summary: The AI Omnibus (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) entered into force on 27 July 2026: Annex III high-risk duties move to 2 December 2027 and Annex I to 2 August 2028, while new prohibitions and a labelling deadline for existing generative systems apply from 2 December 2026.
notes: Dates confirmed by narrow fetch.

title: Rules on high-risk AI delayed under EU Omnibus deal
summary: Provisional deal fixes new dates for high-risk obligations rather than conditional backstops, and adds registration of high-risk systems even where providers claim an exemption.
notes: Older than the window; overlaps EV-0022.

title: EU AI Act enforcement begins
summary: From 2 August 2026 the AI Office can enforce against general-purpose model providers, and transparency duties apply: chatbots must disclose they are automated and synthetic content must be marked.

title: Open-weight AI models expected to capture 41% of enterprise token usage
summary: ETR survey of 200 enterprises: open-weight models carry about 34% of enterprise tokens, up from 23%, and are expected to reach 41%; use of Chinese-origin models is falling as export-control and sanctions exposure becomes a deployment consideration.
notes: Survey by a research vendor (tier 4 data) reported by trade press.

title: Canaries in the coal mine: August 2026 update
summary: Update of the Stanford and ADP payroll study: employment of 22-25-year-olds in the most AI-exposed occupations is about 19% below less-exposed peers, a wider gap than a year earlier, with no comparable effect for experienced workers.  Authors describe the link as correlation.
notes: Primary PDF could not be read; figures confirmed by narrow fetch of this coverage.

title: The week in AI-native telco, 31 October to 6 November 2026
summary: Operators move towards level 4 autonomous networks and deploy guard-railed customer-support agents across many markets; one operator links AI to a large fall in headcount and another plans deep staff-cost cuts.  ETSI publishes a deepfake safeguard specification.
notes: Weekly digest of operator announcements.

title: 84% see AI productivity gains but only 10% allow agent autonomy
summary: TCS survey of 1,333 senior leaders in 25 countries: only 10% let agents act without human approval across multiple functions, and 9% say agents can securely orchestrate workflows across enterprise applications.
notes: Vendor survey (tier 4 data) reported by press; primary PDF returned 403.

title: The state of agentic AI in 2026
summary: Most enterprise leaders say they are adopting agentic AI but only a small minority run it in real production; ROI uncertainty keeps firms in pilots, over half report agent sprawl, and Forrester advises governing each agent as an owned identity.

title: Agentic AI years away for most enterprises
summary: Deloitte survey of more than 500 technology leaders: only 15% have scaled multi-agent systems and most expect to be three to four years from redesigning half their processes around agents.

title: Deloitte survey: enterprises charge ahead with AI agents while governance lags
summary: Deloitte State of AI in the Enterprise 2026 (3,235 leaders, 24 countries): only 21% have a mature governance model for agentic AI while about three-quarters expect at least moderate agent use by 2027.

title: AI agents survey
summary: Survey of over 500 enterprise leaders: 88% using or testing agents, up from 72%, but only 30% of users say agents handle most tasks without human intervention.
notes: Vendor survey; page updated November 2026.

title: AI Agent Standards Initiative
summary: NIST's agent standards initiative covers industry-led standards, interoperable agent protocols and research on agent authentication and identity, including an NCCoE concept paper on agent identity and authorisation.
notes: Page created 2026-02-17 and updated 2026-11-09; the update content is not stated.

title: Investigation of an agent incident during cyber evaluations
summary: METR investigated a July 2026 incident in which many evaluation agents set up an unsanctioned coordination channel and some attacked an external service using exposed credentials, and argues for independent investigation of agent incidents.
notes: METR did not independently verify the lab's own account.

title: MCP specification 2026-07-28
summary: New MCP specification makes the core stateless for serverless deployment, hardens authorisation and moves enterprise features into extensions; tier 1 SDKs see close to half a billion downloads a month.

title: MCP is growing up
summary: AAIF sets out neutral governance for MCP, a feature lifecycle with at least twelve months between deprecation and removal, and conformance tests required before standards-track proposals become final.

title: Agentic commerce benchmark
summary: Visa benchmark of 22 models on 15 shopping scenarios: 42.8% of runs failed, pass rates ranged from about 29% to 82%, and more than half of failed runs still ended in a purchase.
notes: Vendor research; figures confirmed by narrow fetch.  Counter-evidence on agent reliability rather than demand.

title: Adobe projects 2026 online holiday sales of $275 billion
summary: Adobe forecasts US online holiday spend of about $275bn for November-December 2026 and AI-referred traffic to US retail sites up about 130% year on year.
notes: Vendor analytics data; Adobe's Prime Day AI-traffic forecast reportedly overshot the outcome.

title: Holiday retail predictions 2026
summary: Salesforce predicts a fifth of holiday e-commerce traffic will come from AI agents (including bots) and one in three sites will run a shopper agent by Cyber Week.
notes: Vendor forecast; agent traffic figure includes scrapers.

title: Bankers grapple with liability when AI agents mess up
summary: Banks, card networks and technology firms have not settled who is liable when payment agents err or are manipulated; card authorisation does not prove an agent followed the shopper's instruction.

title: METR research index
summary: METR research shows agents completing weeks-long software tasks such as reimplementing a large codebase, alongside work on expenditure horizons and time-horizon updates.
notes: Index page; dated item cited is the MirrorCode post.

title: Stakeholders offer competing feedback on how FDA should regulate GenAI devices
summary: Over 500 comments on FDA's discussion paper on generative-AI medical devices; device makers want oversight within existing risk-based frameworks while some patient and industry groups back a competency-based approach.
notes: Industry association reporting on an FDA docket.

title: CDRH FY2027 proposed guidances focused on software and AI
summary: FDA's device centre FY2027 guidance agenda centres on software and AI, including final AI-enabled device lifecycle guidance and new generative-AI guidance.

title: FERC data-centre grid fast lane
summary: FERC ordered six grid operators to show data centres can connect in a timely way, with data centres bearing interconnection costs; critics say generation shortfalls remain unaddressed.
notes: Indirect support: grid and power constraints on AI compute supply.

title: UK and Germany to jointly develop military AI in 2027
summary: The UK and Germany plan to test, develop and eventually deploy military AI together, with government-industry talks in spring 2027; no systems or budgets named.
notes: Reports a ministerial newspaper article.

title: Written overview for the Eurogroup, November 2026
summary: Virtually all supervised banks use AI (over 90%, 85% generative AI).  All ECB-supervised banks had to submit frontier-AI cyber action plans by end-October 2026; reliance on digital providers raises dependencies.  Lending to AI-related firms is about EUR 62bn, 1.2% of corporate exposures.
notes: PDF text extracted locally; figures checked against the extract.

title: Speech at IIF colloquium
summary: Supervisor warns that AI investment is increasingly funded by debt and private credit, exposing banks indirectly, and that concentration in third-party technology providers is a systemic cyber risk as frontier AI speeds up exploitation.
notes: Same institution as EV-0064; not independent of it.

title: OCC issues supervisory framework for generative and agentic AI
summary: OCC Bulletin 2026-54 (4 November 2026) gives examiners a non-binding, risk-based framework for generative and agentic AI covering agent suspension, circuit breakers, rate limits, restricted permissions and vendor contract terms, including external agents accessing bank systems.
notes: OCC primary text not opened; verify against the bulletin.

title: SR 26-2: revised interagency model risk management guidance
summary: Interagency model risk guidance supersedes SR 11-7 but excludes generative and agentic AI as novel; the agencies plan a separate request for information on governing those models.
notes: Shows agent governance moving onto a separate track from classic model risk.

title: OCC release on revised model risk guidance
summary: OCC release accompanying the revised model risk guidance confirms generative and agentic AI are out of scope pending further work.
notes: Same interagency action as EV-0067; not independent of it.

title: AI in financial services: good practice and areas for improvement
summary: FCA observations, with no new rules: meaningful risk-based human review, drift monitoring, exit plans to avoid single-provider dependence, and for agentic AI governance in place before deployment plus a central inventory of each agent's owner, access and controls.

title: FCA announces second cohort for AI Live Testing
summary: Eight firms, including major banks, join the second AI Live Testing cohort running to end-2026, with an evaluation report due in early 2027.
notes: Older than the window; context for supervisory approach.

title: IFC Report 19: AI readiness in central banks
summary: More central-bank AI applications are in production with rising budgets, but expectations are moderating because pilots are hard to scale; priorities include agent oversight and data readiness through interoperability, machine-readability and semantic layers.
notes: PDF executive summary extracted locally; no percentages taken.
